title: Activation Watchtower — Operational Notes & KPI Sandbox
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight working notebook for the Activation Watchtower concept — a small operational surface that combines KPI simulations, gate decision heuristics, and a minimal runbook for staggered rollouts. Aim: make prelaunch decisions reproducible and make tradeoffs explicit (latency vs cost vs quality).

High-level idea:
- Single page of signals (watchtower) fed by short rolling windows (1m/5m/1h) and a probabilistic simulator that shows what happens to KPIs at 10k, 100k, 1M daily requests.
- Signals are grouped: performance (p50/p95 latency, error rate), correctness (eval pass rate on smoke prompts), cost (CPU/GPU tokens per minute), capacity (in-flight requests, queue depth).
- Each signal has: baseline, alert threshold, and a degradation slope used by the simulator.

KPI sandbox (current starting points, tuned from last beta):
- p95 latency (ms): baseline=180, yellow=250, red=400
- error rate (% 5xx/timeouts): baseline=0.4, yellow=1.2, red=3.0
- smoke-eval-pass (%): baseline=97, yellow=94, red=88
- cost per 1k tokens (USD): baseline=0.85, expected surge +30% at 1M/day
- cache-hit-rate (%): baseline=22, yellow=10, red=5
- KV cache evictions/s: baseline=0.8, yellow=1.8, red=3.5

Simulator scenarios (quick notes for runs to push to the gsheet):
1) Organic surge: traffic doubles over 2h, median seq length stable. Simulate batching efficiency lost (batch size 1.3 -> 1.0) => p95 up 45ms, cost +12%.
2) Long-context flash: 20% of requests spike to +3x sequence length. Model kernel path shift increases p95 by 30% and cost +24%.
3) Failure cascade: regional db outage increases error routing to fallback models; increases overall error rate 2.2% and p95 jitter.
4) Adversarial prompt set: smoke-eval-pass drops by 6% on a particular prompt cohort — tie this to A/B rollback.

Gate decision heuristics (working):
- Green: all signals within baseline + 1 sigma for 30m. Proceed with traffic increase +20%.
- Yellow (soft alarm): any two signals breach yellow for 15m OR one signal breaches red briefly. Freeze automated ramp, open on-call, run fast mitigations (restart worker pool, increase dedicated routing to Reserved).
- Red (hard alarm): any critical signal breach red for >5m (p95>red OR error rate>red OR smoke-eval-pass<red). Immediately trigger rollback to previous canary, traffic cut by 50% in 5 minutes, notify exec+SRE.

Owner map and quick tasks (short owner bullets):
- Release lead: Marco Diaz — run daily sims for 3 days pre-surge, coordinate canary window, approve gate thresholds.
- SRE/infra: Linnea Johansson — prewarm dedicated pool, validate autoscale policies, confirm alerting channels.
- Product ops: Aisha Patel — maintain watchtower dashboard, interpret KPI deltas, own stakeholder comms.
- Model ops: Ethan Ross — validate smoke prompt set, snapshot model versions, confirm quantization profile on staging.

Prelaunch checklist (smoketest & soft checks, ticking in order):
- [ ] Canary images built and pinned (model + serving runtime) — GH PR: rollout-scripts/pull/82
- [ ] Smoke eval suite run (1000 prompts) — goal pass >= 96%
- [ ] Autoscale policy dry-run in staging, simulate 3x traffic
- [ ] KV cache priming script executed (top 500 prefixes)
- [ ] Latency baseline established in perf-run-2025-11-01 report
- [ ] Cost estimate for 1st week traffic published to finance (sheet link in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Incident channel & on-call rotation posted (Slack thread: #prodops-launch-2025)

Runbook snippets (put these in the proper runbook later, but keeping here for quick copy):
- If p95 climbs into yellow: restart N smallest workers first (node labels: batch-worker-small), wait 90s, if no improvement escalate.
- If cache-hit-rate drops >10pt: trigger prefix reindex job and rollback cache-clean policy.
- If smoke-eval-pass drops below yellow: immediately shadow new requests to control group, collect 1000 failure examples, pause rollout.

Contingency ideas (low effort, high ROI):
- Temporary response-length cap at the API gateway for first 30s of surge to avoid long-tail tokens draining capacity.
- Route 10% of traffic to a cheaper quantized variant automatically if cost per 1k tokens exceeds threshold.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self and team):
- What is the SLA/contractual threshold that forces exec notification vs standard on-call? (need legal/product ops alignment)
- Do we want automated partial rollback (traffic cut + model variant swap) or manual only? (pros/cons: automation speed vs blast radius)
- Add a synthetic traffic generator that mimics real user seq length distributions (we currently use uniform).
- Where to store canonical failure examples for postmortem; Confluence page exists but needs stable ID (linked_artifacts).

Immediate next steps (for this doc):
- Marco: run the 3 core simulator scenarios and upload results to gsheet by 2025-11-07.
- Linnea: dry-run autoscale policy and validate prewarm scripts by 2025-11-05.
- Ethan: finalize smoke prompt set and push snapshot tag v2025-11-01.
- Aisha: create a lightweight dashboard (Grafana) with the 6 signals above and invite on-call.

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. This doc is the sandbox for gating heuristics — when we stabilize, copy into product-ops canonical playbook and link from release-readiness artifacts.

---
Choppy brainstorm fragments below (retain for context):
- signal decay windows: 1m/5m/1h, but alarm windows differ: latency->5m, error rate->1m, smoke->30m
- tie cost alarms to forecast curve rather than instantaneous cost (avoid false positives)
- consider user cohort bucketing for smoke-eval (new vs returning vs pro customers)
- thought: automatic sample of failed responses to S3 for quick triage (index by ticket id)

End of doc.
